name: ArtOnBar — specialty coffee in the Algarve
description: Every café on artonbar.com/coffee/ with town, type, hours, opening time, Sunday opening, roaster, oat milk, laptop- and dog-friendliness, price, rating (source stated), whether we visited, and coordinates.
license: Free to use with attribution and a link to artonbar.com

cafes.name: Mellow Café
cafes.desc: One of only two places in Loulé where the coffee is made properly. A small, vintage-looking room with mismatched china, good homemade cakes by the slice, and cocktails later in the day. Took over the old Cinnaroma bakery premises.

cafes.name: bean17 coffee and more
cafes.address: Mercado Municipal de Loulé, loja 11, Rua Ataíde de Oliveira
cafes.desc: The coffee counter inside Loulé's market, roasting its own beans: the other properly made cup in town, with single-origin espresso, pour-over, Dutch apple pie and banana bread. Mornings only, cash only, tiny. A morning plan.

cafes.name: The Showroom Coffeehouse
cafes.desc: Almancil's proper coffee, Australian-style, in a design showroom: flat whites on Amsterdam-roasted beans, matcha, cinnamon buns, Wi-Fi and dogs welcome. Weekdays only, few seats outside.

cafes.name: Lahana
cafes.desc: Espresso, batch brew and açaí bowls at a small counter in an outdoor plaza near Quinta do Lago, under the bougainvillea. Open every day from eight, which nothing else around here is; recent complaints about brusque service and paper cups.

cafes.name: Café Calcinha
cafes.desc: The 1929 art-deco grand café on the square, restored and municipality-owned, with the Folhado de Loulé pastry. You come for the room and the long hours; the coffee is fine rather than remarkable, and service drifts.

cafes.name: Melbourne Lane Cafe
cafes.desc: The specialty coffee and brunch most people in Faro rate first: Aussie-style, bagels and waffles, always busy. Free Wi-Fi, no stated laptop policy.

cafes.name: Yellow Bourbon Specialty Coffee Bistro
cafes.desc: The bistro in the yellow building near the old town, pouring beans roasted at its own roastery 150 metres away. Terrace, pastries, gluten-free and vegan options; the warm dishes are the weaker part.

cafes.name: Yellow Bourbon Roastery & Store
cafes.desc: The roastery itself, with an espresso bar: pick your bean (Brazil, Colombia, Ethiopia, Guatemala), good decaf, bags to take home. Two flat whites about €7.

cafes.name: Evolution Brunch
cafes.address: Rua Eng. Aboim Sande de Lemos 1
cafes.desc: Spacious brunch room north of the centre, attached to an EV showroom, listed on Google as a coworking space and easy to work from. Great plates; nobody writes about the coffee itself, so we haven't ranked it on that.

cafes.name: Pastelaria Padaria Centeio
cafes.desc: Opens at seven. Fresh pastel de nata (€1.50), Faro's own Dom Rodrigo egg sweets and a galão at the counter. The seven-o'clock answer.

cafes.name: Pastelaria Coelho
cafes.desc: Pastelaria and cheap-lunch institution open from seven until midnight: bifana, nata, a decent cappuccino, slow when it's full.

cafes.name: Café Tinto
cafes.desc: Olhão's one specialty coffee bar, opened in 2024 by Mo and Talia, 5.0 on Google from hundreds of reviews: beans scored 85+, deli sandwiches, oat milk, dogs welcome. Tiny, a declared laptop-free zone, and shut by two.

cafes.name: Casa Amor
cafes.desc: The ground-floor café of a ten-room townhouse hotel run by Parisian owners, known in town for French pastries. A calm, pretty room; specialty credentials unverified, so it's here for the pastries.

cafes.name: Cantaloupe Vol.2 Jazz Café
cafes.address: Mercado da Verdura, Av. 5 de Outubro, Loja 47
cafes.hours: Roughly Mon & Wed–Thu 10:00–20:00, Fri 10:00–22:00, Sat from 15:00, Sun from 17:00, closed Tue (sources differ)
cafes.desc: Waterfront terrace on the Ria Formosa, new owners since August 2026, live jazz on Sundays. Coffee treated with respect rather than specialty-sourced; the view does the rest.

cafes.name: Kubidoce
cafes.desc: Pastry chef Filipe Martins's bakery on the N125: the pastel de nata most of Olhão calls the best, and the Folar de Olhão. The coffee is the weak link; the pastries are the point.

cafes.name: Pastelaria Bijou
cafes.desc: Tiny local café below the church: toast, orange juice and a galão for two for about €10, shaded tables outside, cash only.

cafes.name: Xisto
cafes.address: Av. Dr. Mateus Teixeira de Azevedo 48
cafes.desc: The best coffee and the best croissants in Tavira, with real sourdough and gluten-free seeded bread, on a three-day week. Queue at nine, few seats; laptop-tolerant, dogs fine.

cafes.name: Café Formosa
cafes.desc: Riverside towards the ferry quay: 'best flat white in Tavira' in review after review, in-house low-sugar cakes, matcha and kombucha, free Wi-Fi. The complaint is always the same: why not open before nine.

cafes.name: The Table Coffee (at NŌMA)
cafes.desc: Tavira's coffee-and-cowork, now a morning pop-up inside NŌMA: flat whites, V60, big shared tables, Wi-Fi, dogs inside. The old standalone café on Rua 25 de Abril is gone; the website still shows it. Closes at one.

cafes.name: Originato
cafes.desc: Riverside coffee-and-brunch with latte art, oat cappuccinos and pancakes, and the only specialty room in Tavira open all afternoon, every day. Busy at peak.

cafes.name: Flavour Café
cafes.desc: The early opener on the river square: a long coffee and tea list, oat cappuccinos, cakes and fast service from half past seven. Not third-wave, reliably open.

cafes.name: Snack Bar Alagoa
cafes.desc: Cheap drinks and toasties on the Jardim da Alagoa with, as one reviewer put it, the best morning sun in winter.

cafes.name: The Studio (old town)
cafes.desc: Roasts its own beans in-house, opens at seven, and has a dedicated coworking bar with sockets. The most work-ready specialty café in the Algarve; no sign outside, so trust the address.

cafes.name: The Studio (marina)
cafes.desc: The Studio's second Lagos site with a mini roastery you can watch, batch brew and a gluten-free almond-orange cake. Small, and the easiest Studio to reach without cobbles.

cafes.name: DOT Coffee
cafes.desc: The highest-rated coffee in Lagos: a few tables, properly textured milk, vegan pastries, guest roasters from Rotterdam and Portugal. A sign asks you not to camp all day with a laptop.

cafes.name: Everyday People Coffee
cafes.desc: Marina side, outside the cobbles: a separate free coworking room, rotating European roasters, oat milk at no extra charge, cookies and sandwiches rather than pastries. The cyclists' and remote workers' pick.

cafes.name: Black and White
cafes.desc: The busiest brunch in the old town, with a takeaway counter next door that skips the queue. Laptops only on the window stools, by design. Year-round and consistent.

cafes.name: Coffee & Waves
cafes.hours: Tue–Sun 09:00–16:00; closed when the surf is good
cafes.desc: Lagos's original third-wave bar: a walk-up window, guest roasters from Koyo to Friedhats, bags for sale, açaí bowls. A few bar seats, pricey, and the least predictable hours in town.

cafes.name: Alex
cafes.desc: Coffee, brunch and wine at the edge of the old town, near the bus station: Wi-Fi, air conditioning, dogs inside, cinnamon buns, and no queue.

cafes.name: Twin Fin
cafes.desc: Surf café with big communal tables, savoury waffles and banana bread, Wi-Fi and dogs inside. Now on a four-day week, so check the day.

cafes.name: Abigail's Cafe
cafes.desc: Big vegetarian brunch terrace with juices, vegan and gluten-free everything, beans from a Lisbon roaster. Walk-ins only and very busy.

cafes.name: The Studio (Luz)
cafes.hours: Daily from 07:00 or 07:30 (sources differ) to mid-afternoon
cafes.desc: The only verified pre-eight coffee between Lagos and Sagres, roasting on site, on the road cyclists ride out on.

cafes.name: Matilda Café
cafes.desc: New in autumn 2026: fruity espresso, cold brew, natural wine in the evening. Fifteen reviews so far, all glowing. Promising, not yet proven.

cafes.name: Padaria Central
cafes.desc: The bakery since 1926: thirty pastries, a nata with runny custard (€1.90), take a number, cash only. The traditional seven-o'clock stop.

cafes.name: Velochique Vista Rio
cafes.desc: The riverfront sister of Monchique's cycling café, and the best coffee in Portimão proper: batch brew and espresso with latte art, lemon tart, bike parking out front.

cafes.name: Nomads Specialty Coffee
cafes.address: Av. Tomás Cabreira, Ed. Varandas da Rocha 81, loja 26
cafes.desc: An e-scooter rental with a serious coffee corner: Al-Gharb beans from Albufeira, flat white €3.20, oat or almond for 20 cents more, homemade cookies. A stand rather than a lounge, and one of the few things on the strip open all winter.

cafes.name: Rocha Beach House
cafes.address: Av. Tomás Cabreira, Ed. Rochamar, loja 5
cafes.desc: Surf shop, poké bar and a real coworking room with adjustable desks, fast internet and a phone booth, day passes available. Opens late, at ten.

cafes.name: Coffeine & Brunch
cafes.desc: American-style brunch a street back from the strip, gluten- and dairy-free pancakes, oat lattes (small ones), Wi-Fi and outlets. Good coffee by reviewers' accounts; no specialty sourcing stated.

cafes.name: Wild's Sandwich Boutique
cafes.address: Rua Quinta da Praia, lote 4, loja 8
cafes.desc: Irish-run sandwich and brunch bar between Alvor village and the beach, self-described specialty coffee, cinnamon buns and bagels cooked to order. 'Four dogs this morning', says a review approvingly.

cafes.name: Cult n' Art Café
cafes.desc: The highest-rated café in Alvor: brunch, sourdough from the village bakery, kombucha, an art shop, €1 espresso. Not specialty-sourced, and nobody minds.

cafes.name: Clarice's
cafes.hours: Closed for winter; reopens 5 January 2027 (then Tue–Sat 08:30–15:00)
cafes.desc: Japanese soufflé pancakes and cinnamon buns in Alvor village, closed until 5 January 2027. Reviews praise the food and grumble about rushed service.

cafes.name: Pastelaria Arade
cafes.desc: One of the oldest pastelarias in Portimão: Dom Rodrigo, almond cake, natas, and a coffee reviewers keep calling amazing for what it is.

cafes.name: Clifftop Coffee Roasters
cafes.desc: A roastery, not a café: roasts weekly since 2021 and supplies cafés across the Algarve. Worth a line for residents buying beans.
